name: Flatskin — The Aug-Rejection Youth Movement
description: Flatskin is a youth-driven identity movement that rejects all augmentation — cyberware, geneware, and BCI — as a form of corporate colonization of the body. Members called Flats wear undyed natural-fiber clothing, keep unmodified bodies, and mark themselves with hand-tattooed geometric patterns using non-digital instruments as the only accepted form of body alteration. The movement has a paradoxical class dimension: in Tier 1 where augmentation is often medical necessity, Flatskin is a privilege statement; in Tier 3-4 where aug is social expectation, it's genuine rebellion. The internal split between 'Hard Flats' (who condemn all aug including medical) and 'Soft Flats' (who accept medical necessity) is a constant source of community conflict.
cultural_impact: Flatskin's visibility has provoked backlash from aug-positive communities and medical device corponations simultaneously, while their hand-tattooing practice has spawned a cottage industry of Flat tattoo artists who charge premium rates to Tier 3 members seeking authentic marks.
locations: Flat House Community Space, Tier 2 West Corridor
Flatskin Forum, Underworld (accessed via non-aug terminal)
story_hooks: A Flatskin Hard Flat leader is secretly receiving treatment for a degenerative condition that requires augmentation to survive — and the community's discovery of this could fracture the movement entirely.
A corponation is funding a Flatskin splinter group to radicalize the movement toward violence against aug clinics, creating a pretext to crack down on the broader aug-rejection community.
A Shelf kid who needs a medical aug to survive is being pressured by a Flatskin Hard Flat chapter in her neighborhood — and the players must navigate community politics without getting anyone killed.
